candidates.name: d1r0A
candidates.idea: Give the segment labels the most space, using content-sized numeric columns to limit row wrapping.
candidates.label: gold

whys: The wider segment column keeps Community solar on one line and gives the other labels natural breaks. All values fit and the table is compact; unequal quarter widths slightly weaken the regular grid.

Row labels wrap at natural boundaries, while all headers and numbers remain whole. The wider label column supports quick lookup, although the uneven numeric column widths make the quarter grid slightly less regular.

The wider segment column keeps Community solar on one line and leaves only two naturally wrapped labels. All figures fit and are easy to scan; the unequal quarter widths slightly weaken the otherwise clear repeated structure.
All text and numbers fit, and equal quarter columns make comparisons straightforward. Natural wraps in three segment labels create taller rows and leave the label column somewhat cramped.

Equal numeric columns make the quarter grid regular and easy to compare. The narrower label column adds a third wrapped row and separates the ampersand from Commercial, making the stub less fluent than in A.
All content fits, and the equal quarter columns make comparisons easy. Three segment labels wrap naturally, though the extra height in the Community solar row makes the body less compact.

candidates.name: contrast
candidates.idea: Equal columns leave only 48 px of text space for segment labels. That is too narrow for the longest unbreakable label unit and would force awkward breaks or overflow, while giving short numeric entries unnecessary space.
candidates.label: bad

whys: Segment and several row labels still break inside words, making lookup difficult and producing tall, uneven rows. Community solar wraps slightly less severely than in C.

The slightly wider stub reduces some fragmentation and row height compared with C, but Segment and multiple row labels still break inside words. The resulting tall, sparse rows impair lookup and visual rhythm.
The segment column still breaks the header and multiple labels inside words. Community solar occupies fewer lines than in C, but the tall, sparse rows remain difficult to scan.

The narrow segment column splits the header and several labels within words, including Residential rooftop and Commercial & industrial. The resulting tall rows make labels hard to scan and leave large empty areas beside the numbers.

The narrow stub splits Segment and several row labels inside words, including Residential and Commercial. Tall rows and large empty numeric cells make scanning and matching labels to values difficult.

The narrow segment column splits the header and several labels inside words, including Residential rooftop and Commercial & industrial. Tall rows and large empty numeric cells make lookup and comparison laborious.

d1.purpose: Show 2024 solar PV capacity additions in MW by market segment, country and quarter, with totals for each country-quarter.
tasks: Find an addition value for a particular segment, country and quarter.
Compare Q1 with Q2 within a country and compare countries within or across regions.
Read across a segment or down a country-quarter column, including the total.
relations: Each region groups two countries; each country groups Q1 and Q2.
Each data cell connects a segment with one country and quarter; the total summarizes the segments above it.
roles: The first column identifies segments and the total.
Three header levels identify region, country and quarter.
The eight data columns contain comparable MW values.
keep_whole: Country and region names where their merged headers allow it.
Quarter labels, individual numbers and the words in segment names.
may_wrap: Multiword segment names at spaces; Commercial & industrial can use multiple lines.
same_scale: The eight quarter columns serve the same role and should remain broadly comparable in width.
Paired quarters within each country should have similar widths.
d1.h_vs_v: The width limit requires segment labels to wrap. Giving the first column more space shortens rows but leaves the numeric columns close to their content minimum; giving it less space creates more vertical reading while allowing a more even data grid.

d2.purpose: Show quarterly solar PV capacity additions by market segment across four countries in 2024, in MW.
tasks: Find a segment’s additions for a country and quarter.
Read country-quarter totals alongside segment values.
relations: Each region contains two countries; each country has Q1 and Q2 columns.
Each segment row contains comparable values across all eight country-quarter combinations.
The total row aggregates the segment values for each country and quarter.
roles: The first column identifies segments and the total.
Three header tiers identify regions, countries and quarters.
The eight numeric columns carry values in the same unit and have equal analytical status.
keep_whole: Individual words in segment and country names
may_wrap: Multiword segment labels at word boundaries, especially Commercial & industrial and Residential rooftop
same_scale: The eight country-quarter columns should have a broadly similar scale.
Paired quarters within each country should have similar widths.
d2.h_vs_v: The viewport cannot accommodate the widest segment label on one line while preserving all numeric columns. Wrapping some segment labels adds row height but frees space for readable, comparable values.

d3.purpose: Show solar PV capacity additions in MW across market segments, countries and the first two quarters of 2024.
tasks: Look up a segment’s addition for a country and quarter.
Compare quarters within a country and corresponding quarters across countries.
Compare segment contributions with each country-quarter total.
relations: Europe groups Germany and France; Asia-Pacific groups Japan and Australia.
Each country has Q1 and Q2 columns, and each data row supplies values for all four countries.
The Total row aggregates the segments for each country-quarter.
roles: The first column identifies segments and the total; its header spans the three header tiers.
Regional and country headers group the quarterly columns beneath them.
Quarter headers identify the individual measures; numeric cells contain additions in MW.
keep_whole: Country and region names, including Asia-Pacific.
Utility-scale and the other unbreakable units in segment labels.
may_wrap: Multiword segment labels may wrap at spaces, keeping their reading order natural.
same_scale: Quarter columns serve the same role and should have broadly comparable widths, while allowing for differences in numeric content.
Region and country headers derive their widths from their grouped columns.
The segment column needs a different scale from the numeric columns because its labels are longer.
d3.h_vs_v: The viewport cannot accommodate every segment label on one line while preserving all numeric values. Giving the segment column more width can reduce wrapping; giving the quarterly columns more room produces a more open numeric grid at the cost of taller label rows.

analysis.strengths: All headers and values are visible, the geographic and country groupings are clear, and the table fits the viewport exactly. Numeric entries remain on one line, making quarter-to-quarter and country comparisons easy. The two longer segment labels wrap at natural word boundaries.
analysis.faults: The first two data rows are taller than the others, and their labels take two lines. The table uses the full viewport width, leaving no horizontal margin within it.
analysis.spatial_logic: Each numeric column receives the minimum width needed for its widest value, including padding and borders. The remaining width goes to the segment labels. This preserves whole numbers and keeps three of the five row labels on one line.

rounds.insights: The width constraint is decisive: the numeric columns collectively need 461 px to keep their contents whole, leaving 144 px for the segment column within the 605 px column-width budget. Giving the labels more room would force at least one numeric column below its measured one-line requirement. The two natural label wraps are a reasonable trade-off for keeping the comparison values intact.

contrast.why: Equal columns leave only 48 px of text space for segment labels. That is too narrow for the longest unbreakable label unit and would force awkward breaks or overflow, while giving short numeric entries unnecessary space.

sameFunctionGroups.why: All eight columns contain quarterly MW values and should have a consistent visual scale. P keeps them reasonably close while varying widths to fit their different numbers.

synthesis.rationale: P fits the viewport and preserves every visible value and header without breaking words. The two longer segment labels wrap naturally, while the regional, country and quarter headers remain on one line. The quarter columns are similar enough in width to support comparison, and the row labels retain enough space to remain easy to scan.

general: Protect complete words and numeric values before optimizing symmetry or compactness.
Give columns with the same role a consistent visual scale, allowing content-driven variation when space is constrained.
Use merged headers and alignment to make the relationships between groups and values easy to follow.
specific: Allowing two segment labels to wrap makes room for all eight quarterly columns within 606 px.
The shorter values in France and Australia permit narrower columns without forcing breaks.

synthesis.tradeoffs: P uses the full viewport width and makes two body rows taller. Its unequal quarter-column widths slightly weaken uniformity but accommodate the values within the available space.
synthesis.uncertain: Only P was supplied as a candidate, so there is no rendered alternative to compare against it.

critique.good: All content is visible, headers stay on one line, and the segment labels wrap naturally. Keeping Utility-scale and Community solar on one line makes the body compact and easy to scan.
critique.problems: The quarter columns vary noticeably in width, especially the narrow Australia Q1 column beside Q2. Some totals sit close to their cell borders.
critique.cause: The 144px segment column leaves the data columns at their individual content minima; Australia Q1 is 49px while Q2 is 59px.

critique.good: The quarter columns are nearly uniform, making country and quarter comparisons easier. All headers and numbers remain intact, and segment names break at spaces.
critique.problems: Community solar takes two lines, adding a tall row with mostly empty numeric cells. The extra height produces a looser body than A.
critique.cause: The 125px segment column is too narrow for Community solar on one line; the saved width is distributed across the data columns.

critique.good: The quarter columns have a consistent scale, with equal widths within each country. All headers and values remain visible.
critique.problems: Four segment rows occupy two lines, making the body tall and leaving substantial blank space beside the numbers. Utility-scale breaks at its hyphen, interrupting a short label.
critique.cause: The 107px segment column is too narrow for both Utility-scale and Community solar, while the data columns receive 60–65px each.

critique.good: All text is visible, the header hierarchy is clear, and the quarter columns form a broadly even grid. Segment labels wrap at word boundaries.
critique.problems: Three segment rows are two lines tall, leaving more vertical space between values in adjacent rows. The last quarter column is visibly wider than most of its peers.
critique.cause: The 116px segment column forces Community solar onto two lines; the final data column takes 65px.

critique.good: Community solar fits on one line, making the table more compact. All headers and values remain visible, and the two longer segment names break naturally.
critique.problems: The data grid is uneven, especially within Australia, where the first quarter is noticeably narrower than the second. Several totals sit close to their column edges.
critique.cause: The 144px segment column leaves only 461px for the eight data columns; Australia’s quarters receive 49px and 59px.

critique.good: The data columns are consistent in width, supporting comparison across countries and quarters. Labels and values remain intact.
critique.problems: Community solar still wraps, so the additional width given to the segment column does not reduce the table height compared with d1r1A.
critique.cause: At 125px, the segment column is still too narrow for Community solar on one line.

critique.good: All text is visible, headers remain whole, and the country and quarter groupings are easy to follow.
critique.problems: Community solar takes two lines, adding height to a short row label. The Australia quarter columns also look noticeably unequal.
critique.cause: The 140px segment column falls just short of keeping Community solar on one line; Australia’s columns are 52px and 59px.

critique.good: Community solar stays on one line, making the table shorter while preserving whole words, numbers and headers. The hierarchy remains clear and the table fits the viewport.
critique.problems: Australia’s Q1 column looks narrow beside Q2, and the data columns have slightly uneven spacing.
critique.cause: The 144px segment column uses the width needed to keep Community solar whole, leaving Australia’s Q1 at 49px and France’s Q1 at 54px.

critique.good: The quarter columns have a consistent visual scale, supporting comparisons across countries. All text remains visible and whole.
critique.problems: Three segment labels wrap, making the table taller and giving the first column a compressed appearance.
critique.cause: The 125px segment column gives more space to the quarter columns but forces Community solar onto two lines.

critique.good: All content fits, headers stay on one line, and only two segment rows wrap. Community solar and Utility-scale remain intact, making the row labels easy to scan.
critique.problems: The numeric columns vary noticeably in width, especially within the Australia pair. Some totals sit close to cell boundaries, giving the numeric area an uneven rhythm.
critique.cause: The 144px segment column leaves only 49px for Australia Q1, compared with 59px for Q2; France Q1 is also narrower at 54px.

critique.good: The numeric columns have a consistent scale, and paired quarters align comfortably. All values and headers remain whole.
critique.problems: Community solar wraps, adding a tall row and interrupting the otherwise compact run of shorter segment labels.
critique.cause: The 120px segment column is too narrow for Community solar on one line.

critique.good: The numeric columns have comfortable, broadly similar widths, and the headers and values remain whole.
critique.problems: Four segment rows wrap, including Utility-scale at its hyphen. The narrow label column makes the table taller and the row labels less immediately scannable.
critique.cause: The 107px segment column forces both Utility-scale and Community solar onto two lines.

critique.good: All content fits the viewport, numeric values remain whole, and the country-quarter columns have a relatively consistent scale. The three header tiers are clear.
critique.problems: Community solar wraps onto two lines, adding height to an otherwise short row. The extra line makes the body less compact and interrupts the rhythm of the segment labels.
critique.cause: The 132px segment column is too narrow to keep Community solar on one line.

critique.good: All content fits, the header hierarchy remains clear, and Community solar stays on one line. The two longer segment labels wrap naturally, making the body more compact without splitting words or values.
critique.problems: Australia’s Q1 column is noticeably narrower than its Q2 column, and France’s Q1 is also comparatively tight. This makes the quarter columns somewhat uneven, especially in the totals row.
critique.cause: The 144px segment column leaves 49px for Australia Q1 and 54px for France Q1. Both still accommodate their widest values with the specified padding.

critique.good: All content fits, headers stay on one line, and the table uses only two wrapped segment rows. The compact body makes country and quarter comparisons easy.
critique.problems: The numeric grid is tight, especially around the four-digit totals. The narrow Australia Q1 column makes that country pair less even.
critique.cause: The 144 px segment column leaves quarterly columns close to their minimum widths; Australia Q1 is 49 px.

critique.good: All content fits, with intact numbers and single-line headers. Quarterly columns have a little more breathing room than in A.
critique.problems: Community solar wraps, adding a tall row and interrupting the otherwise compact lower half of the table. The extra numeric space is modest relative to that cost.
critique.cause: The 124 px segment column is too narrow for Community solar on one line.

critique.good: All values and headers remain visible, and most quarterly columns have more space for comparisons.
critique.problems: Every segment label wraps, making the body much taller. Utility-scale breaks at its hyphen, separating a unit that should stay together. The tall rows leave large empty areas across the numeric grid.
critique.cause: The 107 px segment column forces the extra wrapping; its width is insufficient to keep Utility-scale on one line.

critique.good: All text and numbers fit, the header hierarchy is clear, and the quarter columns retain enough width for their values. Segment labels wrap at natural spaces.
critique.problems: Community solar wraps unnecessarily, making that row taller and interrupting the otherwise compact lower half of the table. The numeric columns also have uneven whitespace.
critique.cause: The 136 px segment column leaves too little room for Community solar; Germany’s 63 px columns use space needed by the segment column.

critique.good: All content fits without word breaks. Community solar stays on one line, improving the table’s rhythm, while the two longer labels wrap naturally. The grouped headers and country-quarter comparisons remain clear.
critique.problems: The numeric grid is tight, especially around the four-digit totals, and the unequal column widths are visible. Residential rooftop and Commercial & industrial still require two lines.
critique.cause: The 144 px segment column uses the space available after preserving the minimum widths needed for the numeric values; a wider label column would crowd or break those values.
